newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares close mixed, few foreign deals. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russian shares close mixed, few foreign deals. [CORRECTED 17:40 GMT]

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on Tuesday with few foreign orders in sight, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 0.44 points to 174.28.
"Everyone was ready for a fall," said Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director of IK Prospekt. "But there was some money, not very big amounts, and the market stabilised at opening levels."
Foreign investors, he said, were ready to buy big packages at levels slightly lower than current bids, he said.
Ippolitov said prices would fall in the next few days.
UFG trader Maxim Perlin said some Russian brokers were supporting the market on the expectation that prices would rise in the absence of serious sales.
"The fall, which happened after the announcement about the forthcoming operation on (President Boris) Yeltsin, has already been compensated for," he said.
Yeltsin said two weeks ago that he would undergo a heart operation. Prices fell sharply immediately after the announcement.
Traders said investors focused on the second-tier shares and shares of regional companies.
TsUM was one of the main gainers of the day and Ippolitov said its market-makers were driving prices up ahead of placing a new share issue.

TsUM plans to issue 30 million of ordinary shares with a face value of 1,000 roubles on October 1. The price of the placement will be announced on the day of the issue. TsUM closed at $0.35 after $0.29 at Monday's close.
The biggest riser of the day was Izhorskiye Zavody, which was traded at $11.00 after $8.99. The loser of the day was St Petersburg International Telephone, which fell to $8.28 from $8.70.
LUKoil rose to $9.45 from $9.26, UES fell to $0.0779 from $0.0787, Norilsk Nickel rose to $6.75 from $6.70 and Rostelekom edged down to $2.485 from $2.500. (Corrects Norilsk Nickel closing price)
